::: {#sol-best-constant-part2}

At $c = \mean$, the second term is zero,
so the smallest [expected squared error](expectation.qmd#def-squared-error-risk) is $\Var{Y}$.

Under [squared error](expectation.qmd#def-squared-error-loss),
the best [prediction](expectation.qmd#def-prediction) made without any [input](#def-input) is the [mean](expectation.qmd#def-expectation),
and what remains is the [variance](#def-variance).
A prediction that uses an input $X$ can improve on $\Var{Y}$
only through how the mean of $Y$ changes with $X$.
The [conditional expectation function](expectation.qmd#def-cond-expectation-function) describes that change.

:::
